what_it_checks: The published resource of §8.1 and the matching of §8.3 and §9 step 2, offline: given the bytes the origin served for `host`, the operator identifier in question and the instant `now`, whether the document is acceptable at all and which statement, if any, matches — its domain_ascii equals the host, its operator_id is the one in question, its intent is bind, it passes every check of statement_validity, and it is within its window. `checked_statement` names the construction case a party that keeps state registered and is now looking for, and `checked_statement_state` what that party concludes about it: `matched`; `absent` (a valid resource that carries no entry with its digest); `malformed` (the resource is refused, or carries its digest in an entry that fails a check — an unknown state that neither ends nor extends an association); `expired` (carried, and its only defect is that valid_until has passed). Document rules: 8.1-size, 8.1-format, 8.1-entries, 8.1-statement (an element that is not a well-formed statement), 8.2-duplicate. The statements are the construction cases of vectors.json; `body_construction` rebuilds a body from another case's bytes.

cases.label: match
cases.what_it_shows: One statement, by the operator in question, for the fetched host, valid at now.

cases.label: match-among-other-operators
cases.what_it_shows: Two operators declare the host; the other operator's statement is ignored.

cases.label: other-operator-queried
cases.what_it_shows: The same document checked for operator-b.

cases.label: only-other-operators
cases.what_it_shows: Only another operator's statement: nothing matches operator-a.

cases.label: domain-mismatch
cases.what_it_shows: operator-a's valid statement for other.example.org, served at node.example.org.

cases.label: statement-not-yet-valid
cases.what_it_shows: now is five minutes and one second before issued_at.

cases.label: signature-does-not-verify
cases.what_it_shows: The served statement has one bit of its signature flipped.

cases.label: unbind-only
cases.what_it_shows: Only an unbind for the host: an unbind never opens an association (§7.3, §9 step 2).

cases.label: eight-entries
cases.what_it_shows: Eight statements, the most a document may carry.

cases.label: nine-entries
cases.what_it_shows: Nine entries. Nine real statements cannot fit in 65 536 bytes (an ML-DSA-65 key and signature alone take about 7 KiB of base64), so the extra ones are short placeholders: the document stays under the byte limit and only the entry limit refuses it.

cases.label: at-byte-limit
cases.what_it_shows: The `match` document followed by spaces up to exactly 65 536 bytes.

cases.label: duplicate-member-in-statement
cases.what_it_shows: A statement with `sequence` twice inside an otherwise valid document.

cases.label: top-level-array
cases.what_it_shows: An array instead of an object.

cases.label: malformed-entry-beside-match
cases.what_it_shows: The matching statement next to an entry without `domain_binding_method`: one element that is not a well-formed statement makes the whole resource malformed (§8.1), so nothing matches.
